text:
Alice: incident-bot page: high p95 latency for /v1/generate in us-east-1, alerted at 2026-03-15T14:03:10Z. Seeing sustained p95 ~ 1.8s (baseline ~ 350ms). Customers reporting slow responses. Paging oncall (Carla).
Carla: I'm on it. Pulling up dashboards now. Which clusters are affected?
Alice: Traffic is mostly onredwood-gpupool-12 and -13. Canary vs prod mixed. Spike started ~14:00 UTC.
Carla: @Bob @Dan can you join? This looks like a perf regression, possibly infra.
incident-bot: @Carla assigned incident-1765432190 to Carla (oncall). Severity: Sev2. Escalation: 15m.
Bob: Oncall handoff acknowledged. Checking kernel and scheduler metrics from nodes in pool-12.
Dan: I have traces open. Span-level shows token-generation spans elongated; time spent in kernel scheduling appears higher. Attaching top timed traces.
Bob: I see runqueue length jump around 14:00 on several nodes. `runqueue.length` from node exporter: 4 -> 32 on busy nodes.
Eve: Any deploys around the window? I see a kube daemonset kube-proxy update at 13:58 but nothing else.
Alice: No model rollouts at that time; model traffic stable.
Carla: Initial mitigation: I'm shifting requests away from pool-12 to pool-05 via routing policy fallback. Applying canary route now.
Carla: Config: `route_policy weight(pool-05)=1.0 for /v1/generate` (temporary)
incident-bot: Route update applied by Carla. Traffic drain running.
Dan: After routing change p95 dropped to ~420ms on the control plane metrics — looks promising.
Bob: Collecting `perf top` and `sched` counters from affected nodes. Preliminary: lots of time in `__switch_to` and `try_to_wake_up`.
Bob: Kernel version on nodes: 5.19.12-rt vs pool-05 nodes on 5.10.67. There was an infra kernel patch rolled to pool-12 yesterday (5.19.12) for numa scheduler bug.
Alice: That matches timeline. Hypothesis A: kernel scheduler regression in 5.19 causing runqueue pathology under our tokenized workload (many small threads constantly yielding).
Dan: Trace spans show longer syscall latencies for futex/wakeup. Example trace snippet:
```
span gen_token start
  queue_wait: 12ms (was 0.8ms)
  syscall futex_wake: 10ms
  kernel sched: 8ms
span gen_token end
```
Eve: Customer impact: three enterprise tenants reported timeouts >10s for a few requests. CS is messaging impacted customers and throttling heavy batched jobs.
Carla: Mitigations summary in-thread: 1) Route traffic off patched pool (done) 2) Roll nodes back to 5.10 in pool-12 (requires infra; queued) 3) Increase worker-thread batching threshold to reduce scheduling churn (temp config)
Bob: I'm collecting perf counters across 6 nodes and uploading tarball to /mnt/tmp/1765432190/perf.tar.gz
Dan: Adding hypothesis B: small-thread-per-request pattern interacts poorly with `sched_autogroup` and kernel fair scheduler changes in 5.19.
Alice: For RCA we need: timeline, kernel versions, perf samples, trace spans, and request-level logs. I'll start a timeline doc.
Carla: Can someone paste the `dmesg` around 14:00? Looking for scheduler warnings.
Bob: dmesg excerpt:
```
[14:00:03] task redwood-worker-42 blocked for more than 120 seconds.
[14:00:03] INFO: task redwood-worker-42: blocked for 121s, stack trace
[14:00:04] kworker/1:0: CPU#1 stuck for 122s
```
Dan: That is severe. Matches runqueue overload.
Eve: I'm coordinating customer comms: flagged top 5 impacted customers. Sent A1 email templates to CS lead.
Carla: Next steps now: Bob to continue perf collection and start node rollback plan. Dan to collate traces and create minimal repro if possible. Alice to own timeline and postmortem skeleton. Eve to follow up on customer updates.
Bob: Rolling a single node rollback test to 5.10 now (node id gpu-12-07). Will monitor.
incident-bot: Update: rollback job started by Bob at 2026-03-15T14:18:45Z
Bob: Test node shows runqueue back to baseline and token latencies restored after rollback. Rolling remaining nodes in pool-12 in a controlled batch.
Carla: Good. Keep rolling until pool-12 is back to 5.10. After that we'll reintroduce traffic gradually.
Dan: For RCA notes: attach perf flamegraph + a list of top syscalls -> heavy in futex and schedule reschedule.
Alice: Timeline draft:
- 13:58 UTC: infra daemonset update (kmod/kernel patch) started to pool-12
- 14:00 UTC: p95 increase observed, runqueue length increases
- 14:03 UTC: incident page fired, oncall paged
- 14:10 UTC: traffic routed away from pool-12 -> immediate p95 improvement
- 14:18 UTC: rollback test starts on gpu-12-07 -> per-node improvement
- 14:40 UTC: rolling rollback complete; traffic gradually restored; post-incident monitoring
Carla: Will mark Sev2 -> mitigated once all nodes rolled. Keep channel open for RCA handoff.
Eve: CS to send final status update once traffic is 100% restored. Draft ready.
Bob: Uploading artifacts: `/artifacts/1765432190/perf.tar.gz`, `/artifacts/1765432190/flamegraph.svg`, `/artifacts/1765432190/dmesg.txt`
Dan: I'll prepare a minimal repro harness that simulates our worker thread pattern and run it against kernels 5.10 vs 5.19.
Alice: Assigning owners for RCA doc sections: Timeline (Alice), Kernel analysis (Bob), Traces (Dan), Customer impact (Eve), Mitigations & rollout plan (Carla).
Carla: Shout if anyone sees residual p95 blips after full restoration. Otherwise I'll start the postmortem template.
incident-bot: Incident 1765432190 status: mitigated. Handing off to RCA owners. Severity downgraded at 2026-03-15T14:50:02Z.
Alice: Thanks all — we'll reconvene tomorrow for RCA sync at 10:00 PT. Attach any extra logs to the artifacts folder before EOD.
Bob: noted. Saving logs and perf output. Will include `perf report` and kernel config diffs.
Dan: Adding note: also check CFS tunables (sched_latency_ns) differences between kernels.
Eve: CS will send closure notes and customer follow-ups after RCA conclusion.
